# Best MagSafe car mounts (as of Oct 25, 2026)

For most iPhone drivers, I'd pick the **Belkin BoostCharge Qi2 15W vent mount**. Here are the top options from the reviews:

| Pick | Best for | Charging | Price |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Belkin BoostCharge Qi2 Vent Mount** | Most people | Qi2, up to 15W | $47.99 |
| **Anker Prime (A2933, MagGo AirCool)** | Fastest charging, reliability | Qi2 25W, fan + thermoelectric cooling | $89.99 (listed at $69.99 on Amazon in one review) |
| **LISEN Qi2.2 25W with cooling fan** | Fast charging for less | Up to 25W (15W with fan off) | From $39.95 |
| **ESR HaloLock CryoBoost** | Value with a cooling fan | Qi2 15W | $32.80 to $39.99 (see below) |

## Why these
- **Belkin:** It includes a 1-meter USB-C cable and a 27W car adapter, rotates between portrait and landscape, and takes cases up to 3 mm thick. [RottenWiFi](https://rottenwifi.com/best-magsafe-car-mounts-in-2026-connect-charge-and-drive/) and [iTechGuides](https://www.itechguides.com/best-magsafe-car-mounts-in-2026-connect-charge-and-drive/) both name it best overall. Belkin's support documentation says the vent slats must be no more than 3 mm thick and 20 mm deep. Straight horizontal slats work best, and vertical ones can droop.
- **Anker Prime:** [MountGuys](https://www.mountguys.com/best-magsafe-car-mount/) uses it as their daily driver and calls it best overall. It's the priciest, and it doesn't fit Tesla or Mercedes-Benz vehicles, cars without vent blades, or nonstandard vents. Sources disagree on the adapter: MountGuys and [The Gadgeteer](https://the-gadgeteer.com/2026/06/16/best-magsafe-car-mounts-iphone-2026/) say a 60W adapter is in the box, while RottenWiFi says you need a 45W+ adapter for full 25W. Confirm what's included before buying. Only iPhone 17 and 16 Pro Max/16 Plus get the full 25W, and the iPhone 16e isn't supported.
- **LISEN Qi2.2 25W:** The Gadgeteer's best overall pick, with a 95W adapter included. The suction base is large.
- **ESR CryoBoost:** The fan helps prevent heat throttling when running maps in the sun. It's WPC Qi2 certified and mounts on a vent or the dash. ESR's own store lists it at $39.99, and Dealectric reports a code, PARTNER18, took $7.19 off in a cart test on Oct 22. That makes it $32.80, and the code expires 12/31/2026. Checkout has the final word. Dealectric doesn't say whether a car adapter is included, and The Gadgeteer says an 18W adapter isn't, so budget $10 to $15 more.

## Where to buy
- **ESR CryoBoost:** [Buy at ESR's official US store](https://dealectric.com/go/esr-halolock-15w-wireless-car-charger-cryoboost). This is an affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission at no cost to you.
- **Belkin, Anker, LISEN:** The search results didn't include direct product links for these. The review pages above link to Amazon listings for them: [RottenWiFi](https://rottenwifi.com/best-magsafe-car-mounts-in-2026-connect-charge-and-drive/), [The Gadgeteer](https://the-gadgeteer.com/2026/06/16/best-magsafe-car-mounts-iphone-2026/) and [MountGuys](https://www.mountguys.com/best-magsafe-car-mount/).

## Before you buy
- Look for **Qi2 certification**. A mount that says only "MagSafe-compatible" may charge at just 7.5W.
- Check your **vent style**. If the slats are thin, shallow, or vertical, a dash or windshield mount like the Belkin vent/dash version may suit you better.
- If you have an Android phone, you'll need a magnetic Qi2 or MagSafe-compatible case.

If you tell me your phone model and car, I can narrow it down.
